Thought: Nitroxide-Mediated Polymerization (NMP) is a type of controlled/living radical polymerization that is often used to synthesize polymers with well-defined structures. TEMPO (2,2,6,6-Tetramethylpiperidine 1-oxyl) is commonly used as the nitroxide agent in this process. A known characteristic of polymers synthesized via NMP is that they are capable of undergoing thermally induced depolymerization at elevated temperatures. This is due to the reversible nature of the nitroxide-mediated mechanism, which allows for the polymer chains to break down back into monomers when sufficiently heated. Therefore, heating the polymer above 150 degrees Celsius is likely to lead to depolymerization.
